title: VisBench: probing vision backbones across high-, mid- and low-level tasks
description:
VisBench is a unified library for probing vision backbones — DINOv2, CLIP, timm CNNs and ViTs, or a custom nn.Module — across high-level, mid-level and low-level computer vision tasks through one get_backbone() / get_probe() API.

Sixteen probes span object, scene and fine-grained classification, retrieval, semantic and generic segmentation, detection, depth, surface normals, geometric correspondence, mid-level similarity, texture and occlusion edges, 2D keypoints, corners, and gradient orientation. Evaluation protocols are borrowed from prior work rather than re-derived, and cited at the point of use.

Evaluation protocols that cannot be adapted from their original code for licence reasons are implemented from their published descriptions and validated against published numbers — BSDS500’s ODS/OIS/AP boundary protocol reproduces that benchmark’s human agreement. Candidate probes are screened before they are built: a dense probe reads one feature vector per patch, so a target finer than a patch cannot rank backbones however distinctive it is.

Every run writes a structured record under an additive-only schema, and explicit comparability rules decide which records may be ranked together — because the failure this library guards against is not a crash, it is a plausible wrong answer.
